sources.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes
sources.locator: Section 3, PDF pp. 11–16: Hawking effect, free-field propagation on a collapse background, exponential blueshift, and the limits of the reviewed derivation.
sources.reading_extent: Complete 46-page arXiv PDF opened as full text. The complete relevant Section 3 discussion at PDF pp. 11–16 was inspected for this batch; the entire 46-page review is not claimed read.

contents.name: Section 3 review of free-field Hawking radiation and the exponential blueshift near a collapsing horizon
Section 3's physical black-hole temperature and collapse conclusions
contents.reason: This mathematical item proves only the stated one-dimensional test-current model; it does not model collapse, derive a four-dimensional Hawking flux, or assign a physical black-hole temperature.

sources.locator: Section III.A.1–2, PDF pp. 19–22, equations 3.4–3.28 and surrounding assumptions; Section III.A detailed-balance discussion at PDF p. 23, equation 3.40.
sources.reading_extent: Complete 53-page arXiv PDF opened as full text. The complete uniformly accelerated detector reasoning in Section III.A.1–2 and its equation 3.40 detailed-balance discussion were inspected; the entire 53-page review is not claimed read.

contents.name: Section III.A.1–2 uniformly accelerated detector response and its thermal comparison, equations 3.4–3.28
Section III.A detailed-balance relation for excitation and deexcitation rates, equation 3.40
Detector-specific transition probabilities and the infinite-duration rate prescription
contents.reason: The local lemma proves a tested two-point spectral identity only. It does not import the review's detector coupling, infinite-duration probability prescription, or a detector transition-probability theorem.

sources.title: Ted Jacobson, Introduction to Quantum Fields in Curved Spacetime and the Hawking Effect
sources.locator: Section 6.2.1–6.2.3, PDF pp. 32–39: near-horizon exponential relation, positive/negative free-fall-frequency extensions, and thermal mode occupation.
sources.reading_extent: Complete 59-page author-hosted lecture-note PDF opened as full text. The complete relevant Section 6.2.1–6.2.3 development at PDF pp. 32–39 was inspected; no claim is made that every page of the notes was read.

contents.name: Section 6.2.1 near-horizon relation between retarded time and free-fall proper time, equation 6.21
Section 6.2.2 thermal mode occupation with a greybody factor, equations 6.24–6.26
contents.reason: The item proves a one-dimensional chiral two-point spectrum and does not assert the Schwarzschild collapse state, greybody scattering, or a four-dimensional particle flux.

contents.name: Section 6.2.3 exterior thermal state and its near-horizon mode construction
contents.reason: The scoped Fock current is a test-coordinate construction, not Jacobson's black-hole state construction or a full algebraic KMS-state result.

contents.name: §3.1 Definition 3.1 and the continuity estimate for function-defined distributions; §3.2 multiplication and differentiation on distributions
contents.support: The carrier defines the boundary functional on compact smooth tests and uses smooth test-coordinate changes. Grubb supplies the distributional framework; the epsilon-uniform positive-damping estimate is proved in full in the carrier.
